83207a4f-26a0-4063-ae0d-40cc8c31c01b.text_lemmatized: Mitosis has five phases: Interphase, Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, and Telophase.

a1714db3-fb2e-45f1-8062-e1fd32c9c4ac.data: During Interphase, the DNA in the cell is copied in preparation for cell division, resulting in two identical complete sets of chromosomes.
a1714db3-fb2e-45f1-8062-e1fd32c9c4ac.text_lemmatized: During Interphase, the DNA in the cell is copied in preparation for cell division, resulting in two identical complete sets of chromosomes.

10c8de7f-792d-4547-af1c-6257b65ca68f.text_lemmatized: In Prophase, the chromosomes condense into X-shaped structures that can be easily seen under a microscope, and the membrane around the nucleus dissolves away releasing the chromosomes.

c2ee40ab-4c8c-4d11-85fe-0488ca358568.data: During Metaphase, the chromosomes line up neatly end-to-end along the center of the cell, and the mitotic spindle fibers attach to each of the sister chromatids.
c2ee40ab-4c8c-4d11-85fe-0488ca358568.text_lemmatized: During Metaphase, the chromosomes line up neatly end-to-end along the center of the cell, and the mitotic spindle fibers attach to each of the sister chromatids.

84e79d95-d32b-4c12-bf42-deae869b6eac.data: In Anaphase, the sister chromatids are pulled apart by the mitotic spindle, which pulls one chromatid to one pole and the other chromatid to the opposite pole.
